headline: CBA's FY26 result: total operating income of $30,224m, up 6.2% on FY25's $28,465m (ev-1, ev-48); operating performance (pre-provision profit) of $16,469m, up 6.5% from $15,469m (ev-4, ev-49, ev-57); and statutory NPAT of $10,866m beside cash NPAT of $10,982m (ev-8, ev-59). Cash NPAT from continuing operations rose $730m or 7% to $10,982m from $10,252m (ev-7, ev-10, ev-62). Statutory NPAT from continuing operations rose $778m or 8% to $10,911m, and including discontinued operations rose $750m or 7% to $10,866m (ev-11) — the gap to cash is non-cash items: a $62m loss on disposal/acquisition of controlled entities and $54m of hedging and IFRS volatility (ev-59). The bank frames the result as driven by a 6% income increase and 6% underlying expense increase, plus a $62m higher loan impairment expense (ev-10). ROE (cash) rose to 14.0% and cost-to-income improved 20bpts to 45.5% (ev-72, ev-18-source).

drivers.narrative: NII rose $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m, driven by a $92bn or 8% rise in AIEA to $1,246bn, partly offset by a 3bpt NIM fall to 2.05% (ev-19). Home loan averages +$32bn/5% to $630bn, business and corporate +$27bn/10% to $299bn on Business Banking and institutional lending (ev-22, ev-23). Excluding liquids, NIM was stable (ev-24).

Sub-component of the NII bar, not separately quantified in dollars. NIM fell 3bpts to 2.05% (ev-63); excluding liquids growth, which has broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, NIM was stable (ev-24). Asset pricing cut margin 5bpts — home lending pricing 4bpts, business/institutional 1bpt, reflecting competition (ev-20); portfolio mix added 2bpts from business lending and deposit growth (ev-21); funding costs and basis risk flat.

Other operating income rose $196m or 4% to $4,638m (ev-26). Commissions +$135m/6% to $2,234m on higher insurance income including a CommInsure General Insurance sale milestone payment, higher equities income and syndication fees, partly offset by lower deposit fees from fee waivers, lower credit card fees from higher loyalty costs and lower FX (ev-27). Other income +$46m/42% to $156m including a Gemini IPO fair value gain (ev-30); funds management +$12m (ev-31); lending fees +$12m (ev-28); trading income -$9m (ev-29).

drivers.bank_label: Underlying operating expenses (excl. restructuring and notable items)
drivers.narrative: UNDERLYING (not headline) opex rose $719m or 6% to $13,585m (ev-33). The bank's own FY25→FY26 walk: inflation +$455m, investment in technology +$444m, investment in frontline and operations +$128m, other +$96m, partly offset by productivity -$404m (ev-32). By line: IT services +$393m/16% to $2,782m on cloud volumes, software licensing, amortisation and AI/resilience investment (ev-35); staff +$288m/4% to $8,258m with average FTE up 1,760 to 51,756 (ev-34); other +$57m (ev-37); occupancy -$19m on lower depreciation and favourable FX (ev-36).

Restructuring and notable items rose to $170m from $130m, a 31% increase and a $40m drag computed by me from the two annual columns (ev-3). FY26 relates to provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ, an additional goodwill payment to certain customers from ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation; FY25 related to domestic ($52m) and NZ ($33m) remediation plus a Bankwest restructuring provision ($45m) (ev-9, ev-70). These sit outside the underlying expense number.

LIE rose $62m or 9% to $788m — a negative to earnings — with higher collective provisions mainly reflecting portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty (ev-16, ev-42). By division: Retail Banking Services +$106m to $378m on geopolitical risk, macro uncertainty and cost-of-living pressures (ev-43); New Zealand +$11m to $66m on a deteriorating unemployment outlook (ev-46); partly offset by Business Banking -$45m to $310m on lower individually assessed charges including higher write-backs (ev-44) and IB&M -$16m to $33m on individually assessed provision releases (ev-45). LIE to average GLAA up 1bpt to 8bpts (ev-47).

Corporate tax expense rose $208m or 5% to $4,699m — a negative contribution — on the higher pre-tax profit (ev-39). The effective cash tax rate fell 50bpts from 30.5% to 30.0%, primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses in the year ended 30 June 2026 (ev-40, ev-64), so the rate itself was a partial offset to the volume-driven rise. The bank guides FY27 to ~30% (ev-53).

notable_items: FY26 restructuring and notable items of $170m: provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; an additional goodwill payment to certain customers from ASIC's Better Banking review; and domestic customer remediation (ev-3, ev-9)
FY25 restructuring and notable items of $130m: domestic ($52m) and NZ ($33m) customer remediation plus a Bankwest restructuring provision ($45m) (ev-69, ev-70)
Non-cash (statutory-only, NOT bridge drivers): FY26 loss on disposal/acquisition of controlled entities $62m and hedging and IFRS volatility $54m (ev-59); FY25 equivalents $190m and +$53m (ev-61)

disagreements.topic: Cash vs statutory NPAT movement FY26 vs FY25
disagreements.explanation: Cash NPAT excludes non-cash items that management does not consider representative of ongoing performance (ev-60). In FY26 those were a $62m loss on disposal/acquisition of controlled entities and $54m of hedging and IFRS volatility (ev-59), versus $190m and +$53m in FY25 (ev-61). Because the FY25 non-cash drag was larger, statutory profit grew faster than cash. These reconciliation items explain the same-period cash/statutory gap and are NOT year-on-year bridge drivers.

Both documents print $788m FY26 versus $726m FY25, a $62m increase (ev-41, ev-52). The profit announcement rounds the percentage to 9% while the presentation prints 8.5%. Same underlying dollars; the results-book figure ranks higher under the source hierarchy.

disagreements.topic: Operating expense growth rate: underlying vs headline
disagreements.explanation: The bank presents opex on both an underlying and headline basis (ev-27-source). Underlying opex of $13,585m vs $12,866m is +$719m/5.6% (ev-2, ev-33, ev-51); total opex of $13,755m vs $12,996m is +5.8% (ev-54-presentation p54 KPI). The method requires the underlying number as the expense driver with the $40m notables delta claimed separately, which together reproduce the headline movement.

limitations: The bank publishes no single cash-NPAT waterfall for FY26 vs FY25; my bridge is assembled from the Group Performance Summary table's component rows (ev-1 to ev-7) plus the bank's stated component movements. The components sum exactly to the $730m movement, so the residual is zero, but the framing is mine, not a published walk.

The two primary walk charts I adopted are sub-bridges, not the earnings bridge: the results book's underlying operating expense walk (ev-32, sum check passed) decomposes only the $719m expense bar, and the presentation's operating income walk (ev-54, sum check passed) decomposes only the $1,759m income increase into NII and other income.

The NII movement is not split into dollar volume and dollar margin effects by the bank. The nii.volume/nii.margin split is therefore left unquantified in dollars; only the bps NIM walk components are available (asset pricing -5bpts, portfolio mix +2bpts, funding costs and basis risk flat).

The notable-items delta of -$40m is my own subtraction of the two annual columns; the bank prints only the levels ($170m, $130m) and a 31% change, so this contribution is capped below a bank-stated movement.

QUALIFICATION THAT CHANGES MEANING: the reported 3bpt NIM decline is materially a liquids artefact — the bank states that excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, NIM was stable (ev-24). Reading the 3bpt fall as an earnings drag would overstate its effect.

Within the expense walk, the +$455m inflation, +$444m technology and +$128m frontline gross increases are partly funded by -$404m of productivity benefits (ev-32); the $719m net bar hides that gross/offset structure.

Cash NPAT including discontinued operations is also $10,982m in FY26 versus $10,253m in FY25 (ev-61), a $729m movement — $1m different from the continuing-operations $730m. I built the bridge on the continuing-operations basis the bank uses throughout its performance analysis.

I did not read the segment-level income and expense tables, the ASX announcement, or the transcript, so division-level attribution of the income and expense bars beyond what the group narrative pages state is not verified.
Research stopped early: the tool-call budget (40 calls) was reached, so the evidence behind this answer is less complete than a full run's.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income increased 7%, primarily driven by an 8% or $92 billion increase in Average Interest Earning Assets (AIEA). Excluding the impact of liquid assets, underlying Net Interest Margin (NIM) was stable. Average lending interest earning assets increased by $60 billion or 7% due to growth in home, business and institutional lending.

Underlying NIM was supported by higher earnings on replicating portfolio and capital hedges, and favourable portfolio mix, offset by the impact of increased lending price competition and Treasury and Markets.

Other operating income increased 4% primarily driven by higher insurance income and the benefit of one-off gains 3, higher volume driven equities income, partly offset by lower Structured Asset Finance revenue following the sale of the aircraft lease portfolio, lower foreign exchange income, lower deposit fees due to fee waivers and lower credit card fees from higher loyalty costs.

Operating expenses 2 increased 6% mainly driven by inflation, and investment in technology to support infrastructure, resilience and AI capabilities, as well as higher cloud computing volumes and software licensing, and higher staff costs in frontline and operations, partly offset by productivity initiatives and favourable FX.
Loan impairment expense (LIE) increased $62 million, with higher collective provisions mainly reflecting portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty.

CBA delivered a strong FY26 result. Cash net profit after tax increased 7% to $11bn, pre-provision profit increased 6% to $16.5bn and return on equity rose to 14.0%. Operating income increased 6%, supported by customer and volume growth and a broadly stable underlying net interest margin.

Net profit after tax (NPAT) was supported by lending volume growth in our core businesses, with underlying net interest margin broadly stable. This was partly offset by higher operating expenses primarily due to inflation and technology investments, and a higher loan impairment expense due to portfolio growth and increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty.
Investment spend increased 6% to $2.4bn.
